All routes use these so DTO shapes are byte-identical to types.ts.
    37→- Created 9 route files under src/app/api: auth/login, users, conversations, conversations/[id]/messages, events, notifications, notifications/mark-read, company/stats, audit. Every GET has `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`; every route is try/catch → 500 {error}; auth guard via `getAuth(req)` → 401; zod v4 body validation → 400 with friendly message.
    38→- Dynamic route uses Next.js 16 async params: `{ params }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }` + `await params`.
    39→- Login: lowercase/trim email, bcrypt.compare, generic 401 message, writes AuditLog {action:'login'}, returns {token, user: SafeUser}.
    40→- Conversations GET: participants + last message (per-conv take 1) + batched unread counts via `message.groupBy` (senderId != me, read=false), sorted lastMessageAt desc. POST find-or-create is idempotent (verified: two POSTs → same conversation id); rejects self (400) and unknown user (404).
    41→- Messages GET: participant check (403/404), `updateMany` marks incoming unread → read, returns messages asc with senderName. POST: trims text (empty → 400), $transaction [create message + bump lastMessageAt], creates `dm` notification for the other participant with "<senderName>: <text≤80…>"; notification failure is logged, never blocks the send.
    42→- Events GET: job_seeker sees only targetUserId=me; recruiter/company see all; ordered date asc, time asc (string sort — safe for zero-padded formats). POST recruiter-only (403 otherwise): zod regex YYYY-MM-DD + HH:mm (24h), extra `isRealDate` check (2026-02-31 → 400), type enum, target must exist (404) and be a job_seeker (400); creates `event` notification "<creator> scheduled \"<title>\" with you".
    43→- Notifications GET: latest 50 desc + unreadCount. mark-read POST: {ids} or {all:true}, updateMany always scoped `userId = me`; missing both → 400.
    44→- company/stats: single GET computes whole CompanyStats from live queries — funnel via user.count status filters; dmStats per recruiter from fetched messages+conversation participants map; upcomingMeetings date>=today limit 8; pipeline per seeker (SafeUser, earliest future event, unreadDmCount, totalMessages); kpis (eventsThisMonth by YYYY-MM prefix, mostActiveRecruiter by most sent); collectionCounts (6 models); dbLatencyMs timed around `db.user.count()`, dbConnected:true.
    45→- audit GET: latest 50 desc with userName + userRole.
    46→- `bun run lint` → clean. curl-verified every endpoint against the running dev server (no restarts, no reseed). dev.log tail shows only clean compiles, zero errors/500s.

    41→    41→- Messages GET: participant check (403/404), `updateMany` marks incoming unread → read, returns messages asc with senderName. # MASTER PROMPT — Build "TalentBridge_V2"

Copy everything below this line into a new Z.ai chat.

---

You are a senior full-stack engineer. Build a complete, fully working MERN web application named **TalentBridge_V2** that runs 100% on localhost. Do not use any cloud services, paid APIs, or deployments. Prioritize a working end-to-end flow over extra features, but keep the UI clean and modern. Everything below is mandatory unless marked optional.

## 1. Tech Stack & Environment
- **Frontend:** React (Vite) + React Router
- **Backend:** Node.js + Express (REST API)
- **Database:** MongoDB via Mongoose — local instance, connection string in `server/.env` as `MONGO_URI` (default: `mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017/talentbridge_v2`)
- **Run with one command:** root `package.json` using `concurrently` — `npm run dev` starts backend on `http://localhost:5000` and frontend on `http://localhost:5173`
- **Seed script:** `npm run seed` creates all demo users and demo data (idempotent: clears collections, then re-creates)
- **Auth:** simple login form (email + password) issuing a JWT stored in localStorage. No registration page — only the seeded demo accounts can log in. Hash passwords with bcryptjs.

## 2. Roles & Demo Accounts (seed exactly these)
**4 Job Seekers** (View 1):
- `aarav@mail.com` / `123456` — Aarav Sharma (Frontend Developer)
- `priya@mail.com` / `123456` — Priya Patel (Data Analyst)
- `rohan@mail.com` / `123456` — Rohan Mehta (Backend Developer)
- `sneha@mail.com` / `123456` — Sneha Kapoor (Cybersecurity Analyst)

**2 Recruiters** (View 2):
- `recruiter1@mail.com` / `123456` — Nikhil Verma
- `recruiter2@mail.com` / `123456` — Ananya Iyer

**3 Company Users** (View 3):
- `cyber@mail.com` / `123456` — Vikram Rao (Cyber Security Head)
- `eng@mail.com` / `123456` — Dev Menon (Lead Engineer)
- `ceo@mail.com` / `123456` — Meera Nair (CEO)

Login page: one shared login form; after login, route to the correct view based on role. Add quick-login buttons under the form that auto-fill each demo account for easy testing.

## 3. View 1 — Job Seeker Dashboard
- Profile summary card: name, title, skills, profile photo placeholder, application status
- **My Calendar:** month-view grid showing events targeted at this seeker, visually flagged/highlighted; clicking an event opens details (title, date, time, type, who created it, notes)
- **Messages:** list of DM threads with each recruiter → opens chat view
- **Notification bell** in the navbar (see Section 6)

## 4. View 2 — Recruiter Dashboard
- Applicant board: cards for the 4 job seekers (name, title, status) with quick actions **Message** and **Schedule**
- **My Calendar:** month-view grid + **Create Event** button. Event form fields: title, date, time, type (Interview / Meeting / Call), notes, and a required dropdown **"For whom"** listing the 4 job seekers — the recruiter must select exactly one
- The created event automatically appears flagged on the selected job seeker's calendar and triggers a notification for them
- **Messages:** DM threads with each job seeker → chat view
- **Notification bell** in the navbar

## 5. View 3 — Company Command Center (shared by Cyber Security Head, Engineer, CEO)
All three company users log into the same command center with these sections:
- **Analytics dashboard:** hiring funnel (Applied → Interview → Offer) as a visual funnel/bar chart with real DB counts; DM activity stats (messages exchanged per recruiter); upcoming meetings list pulled from calendar events
- **Candidate pipeline table:** all 4 applicants with title, status, upcoming event, unread DM count
- **Cyber Security section:** login activity log (who logged in, when — record a log entry on every login) + a simple security checklist card
- **Engineer section:** system status panel — API status, MongoDB connection status, record counts per collection
- **CEO section:** KPI summary cards — total applicants, events scheduled this month, DMs exchanged, most active recruiter
- Company users are read-only observers: they cannot send DMs or create events. Keep this view simple but data-driven.

## 6. DM System (core feature)
- Any job seeker ↔ any recruiter can DM each other in 1:1 threads. Company users have no inbox.
- Messages persist in MongoDB; a thread shows sender name, text, and timestamp in chronological order
- Unread message count per thread + total unread in the bell badge
- Poll for new messages every 3–5 seconds so replies appear without a manual reload
- Sending a message creates a notification for the recipient
- Clicking a DM notification opens that exact thread

## 7. Notifications
- Bell icon in the navbar of View 1 and View 2 with an unread badge count
- Dropdown with two labeled sections: **Messages** (new DMs — envelope icon) and **Calendar** (new events — calendar icon), each row showing who/what/when
- Items mark as read when clicked; badges update on the same polling interval as messages
- Event notifications are created for the targeted job seeker when a recruiter schedules them

## 8. Data Models (Mongoose)
- **User:** name, email, password (hashed), role (`job_seeker` | `recruiter` | `company`), title, skills
- **Message:** conversationId, senderId, text, createdAt, read (bool)
- **Conversation:** participantIds [2 users], lastMessageAt
- **CalendarEvent:** title, date, time, type, notes, createdBy (recruiter), targetUser (job seeker), createdAt
- **Notification:** userId, type (`dm` | `event`), refId, message, read (bool), createdAt
- **AuditLog:** userId, action, createdAt (feeds the Cyber Security section)

## 9. Seed Data
- All 9 users listed above
- 2–3 sample DM conversations with 4–5 messages each (e.g., Priya ↔ Nikhil discussing an interview)
- 2–3 calendar events (e.g., "Interview — Frontend Role" for Aarav, created by Nikhil, dated next week)
- Everything resets cleanly via `npm run seed`

## 10. UI / UX
- Clean, modern design with a fixed sidebar layout per view
- Color coding: Job Seeker = blue accents, Recruiter = green accents, Company = dark/purple accents
- Build the calendar as a simple custom month grid (no heavy calendar library needed); a light chart approach (plain CSS bars or recharts) for the funnel
- Laptop-friendly responsive layout; no mobile-first complexity required

## 11. Deliverables
- Two folders: `/client` and `/server`, plus root `package.json` (`npm run install-all`, `npm run seed`, `npm run dev`)
- `README.md`: setup steps (start MongoDB → install → seed → run) and the demo account table
- Basic error handling: invalid login, DB down, empty states ("No events yet", "No messages yet")

## 12. Acceptance Checklist (self-verify before finishing)
- [ ] All 9 seeded users log in and land on the correct view
- [ ] Recruiter creates an event picking exactly 1 of the 4 seekers; that seeker sees it flagged on their calendar
- [ ] DM works both directions seeker ↔ recruiter without page reload; unread counts are correct
- [ ] Bell shows both DM and calendar notifications; dropdown works; clicking navigates to the thread/event
- [ ] Company view renders funnel, pipeline, and all 3 role sections using real DB data
- [ ] `npm run seed` resets everything; `npm run dev` boots both servers with no errors

Build the complete project now. If anything is ambiguous, make a reasonable choice and keep going — do not stop to ask questions.

Task ID: 2-a
Agent: full-stack-developer
Task: Backend API routes for TalentBridge_V2

Work Log:
- Read worklog.md, prisma/schema.prisma, seed.ts, src/lib/types.ts, src/lib/auth.ts to absorb the frozen contract; did NOT touch DB/seed/package.json/frontend files.
- Added `src/lib/serialize.ts` (new shared server helper): `safeUserSelect` (explicit field list so `password` is never fetched), `toSafeUser` (skills JSON → string[], timestamps → toISOString), `toMessageDTO`, `toConversationDTO`, `toEventDTO`, `parseSkills`, `truncate(80)`. All routes use these so DTO shapes are byte-identical to types.ts.
- Created 9 route files under src/app/api: auth/login, users, conversations, conversations/[id]/messages, events, notifications, notifications/mark-read, company/stats, audit. Every GET has `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`; every route is try/catch → 500 {error}; auth guard via `getAuth(req)` → 401; zod v4 body validation → 400 with friendly message.
- Dynamic route uses Next.js 16 async params: `{ params }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }` + `await params`.
- Login: lowercase/trim email, bcrypt.compare, generic 401 message, writes AuditLog {action:'login'}, returns {token, user: SafeUser}.
- Conversations GET: participants + last message (per-conv take 1) + batched unread counts via `message.groupBy` (senderId != me, read=false), sorted lastMessageAt desc. POST find-or-create is idempotent (verified: two POSTs → same conversation id); rejects self (400) and unknown user (404).
- Messages GET: participant check (403/404), `updateMany` marks incoming unread → read, returns messages asc with senderName. POST: trims text (empty → 400), $transaction [create message + bump lastMessageAt], creates `dm` notification for the other participant with "<senderName>: <text≤80…>"; notification failure is logged, never blocks the send.
- Events GET: job_seeker sees only targetUserId=me; recruiter/company see all; ordered date asc, time asc (string sort — safe for zero-padded formats). POST recruiter-only (403 otherwise): zod regex YYYY-MM-DD + HH:mm (24h), extra `isRealDate` check (2026-02-31 → 400), type enum, target must exist (404) and be a job_seeker (400); creates `event` notification "<creator> scheduled \"<title>\" with you".
- Notifications GET: latest 50 desc + unreadCount. mark-read POST: {ids} or {all:true}, updateMany always scoped `userId = me`; missing both → 400.
- company/stats: single GET computes whole CompanyStats from live queries — funnel via user.count status filters; dmStats per recruiter from fetched messages+conversation participants map; upcomingMeetings date>=today limit 8; pipeline per seeker (SafeUser, earliest future event, unreadDmCount, totalMessages); kpis (eventsThisMonth by YYYY-MM prefix, mostActiveRecruiter by most sent); collectionCounts (6 models); dbLatencyMs timed around `db.user.count()`, dbConnected:true.
- audit GET: latest 50 desc with userName + userRole.
- `bun run lint` → clean. curl-verified every endpoint against the running dev server (no restarts, no reseed). dev.log tail shows only clean compiles, zero errors/500s.

Stage Summary:
- Endpoints live: POST /api/auth/login · GET /api/users(?role=) · GET/POST /api/conversations · GET/POST /api/conversations/[id]/messages · GET/POST /api/events · GET /api/notifications · POST /api/notifications/mark-read · GET /api/company/stats · GET /api/audit.
- Verified response shapes match src/lib/types.ts exactly (SafeUser.skills always string[]; all DateTime fields ISO strings; EventDTO has creatorName/targetUserName/targetUserTitle; ConversationDTO has lastMessage{ text, senderId, createdAt }|null + unreadCount; CompanyStats full shape with dbLatencyMs/dbConnected).
- Sanity numbers after tests: funnel 4/2/1; dmStats Nikhil 5/5/10, Ananya 2/2/4; kpis totalApplicants 4, dmsExchanged 14, mostActiveRecruiter "Nikhil Verma"; collectionCounts users 9, conversations 4, messages 14, calendarEvents 5, notifications 8, auditLogs 8.
- Quirks the frontend agent must know:
  1) GET messages marks the thread read as a side effect (per spec) — fetch unread counts from /api/conversations, not by peeking at messages.
  2) GET /api/events role-scopes silently: seekers get only their events; recruiters/company get all.
  3) All error responses are `{ error: string }` with 400/401/403/404/500 — display `error` directly.
  4) DM notification text is truncated at 80 chars with "…" appended.
  5) Test writes left artifacts: 1 extra conversation (Aarav↔Priya, empty), 3 extra messages (Priya thread), 1 extra event ("System Design Round" 2026-11-20, Nikhil→Aarav), extra notifications, all seeded messages read + priya's thread fully read. Harmless demo data; reseed only if pristine state is required (NOT done here).
